cards.text: Job is still answering his friends, deep in the middle of one long speech. Now he looks back, the way you scroll WAY up in your phone to the old photos from the good days. He says he longs for the months gone by, the days when God watched over him.

cards.question: Job remembers walking through the darkness back in those days. What did he walk by?

cards.text: He remembers his prime, when the friendship of God rested on his tent. My prime was the Millers' counter, edges sharp, absolutely SURE I was the finest-looking stamper in that whole kitchen.

cards.question: Job says that back then the Almighty was still with him, and his ___ were around him.
Job says life was so rich back then that his steps were bathed in cream.

cards.text: Picture Job heading out to the city gate and taking his seat in the public square. Now watch what happens when this man walks in.

cards.question: When the young men in the square see Job coming, what do they do?
When Job arrives at the square, the old men stay in their seats.

cards.text: The princes stop talking and cover their mouths, and the nobles go so quiet their tongues stick to the roofs of their mouths. Friend, when I walk into MY bakery, the oven timer just keeps beeping like it's never MET me.

cards.question: The people who heard Job called him blessed. Why?

answers.text: He rescued the poor who cried out
He owned the finest house in town
He won every battle he fought

cards.question: Job says that back then, a dying man cursed him.
Job says righteousness ___ him, and justice was his robe and his turban.
Job says he served as eyes to the blind. What does he say he was to the lame?

cards.text: He was a father to the needy, and he shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth. Somebody get this man a CAPE.

cards.question: With all that good behind him, what did Job think his future would be?

answers.text: A long life ending in his own nest
A short life ending far from home
A hard life surrounded by enemies

cards.question: Job pictured himself like a tree whose roots spread out to the waters.

cards.text: Job thought his glory would always be new within him and his bow would stay renewed in his hand. And when he gave counsel, men waited in silence, and his speech settled on them like dew.

cards.question: Job says people waited for him the way they wait for ___.

cards.text: If Job smiled at them, they didn't believe it. The light of his face was precious to them.

cards.question: Job chose their course and presided as chief. He says he dwelt as a ___ among his troops.

cards.text: Then Job comes back to right now. Men younger than he is mock him, and friend, getting roasted by folks younger than you is a special kind of OUCH.

cards.question: Job says he would have refused to put these young men's fathers with what?

cards.text: Then Job paints a picture of them: gaunt from hunger, eating mallow and the roots of the broom tree, living among the rocks and in holes in the ground. They'd been banished from among men and driven off the land.

cards.question: And now, Job says, they mock him in ___.
Job says these men keep far from him, but they still spit in his face.
Back in his good days, Job thought his bow would stay renewed in his hand. What does he say has happened to it now?

cards.text: The rabble comes at him from the right, laying snares for his feet and building siege ramps against him. They keep rolling in, as through a wide breach.

cards.question: Job says terrors are turned loose against him. What do they drive away as by the wind?
Job says his soul is poured out within him, but at night his pains finally rest.

cards.text: Job says He grabs him with great force by the collar of his tunic. Then He throws him into the mud.

cards.question: Down in that mud, Job says he has become like dust and ashes.
Then Job speaks straight to God and cries out for help. What does Job say God does?

cards.text: Job tells God He has ruthlessly turned on him and tosses him about in the storm. And Job says he knows God will bring him down to death, the place appointed for all the living.

cards.question: Job looks back at how he treated people in trouble. What does he say he did?

cards.text: Remember God's lamp shining above Job's head? Now Job says when he hoped for good, evil came, and when he looked for light, darkness fell.

cards.question: Back in his good days, the princes and nobles went quiet when Job took his seat in the square. Now he says he stands up in the ___ and cries for help.

cards.text: Job says he has become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.

cards.question: Job says his skin is finally starting to heal.
Job ends by talking about his harp. What is it tuned to now?

cards.text: And that's where Job leaves it for now, friend. He's not done talking, and trust me, this story's not done either.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He rescued the poor who cried out', comes only from Job 29:12. The card cites Job 29:11-12, which adds the setup verse used in the question. That makes the citation wider than the right answer.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The card says 'Job says He grabs him... Then He throws him into the mud' without saying who 'He' is. The card before it is a choice card about terrors, and God isn't named until card 12 ('Then Job speaks straight to God'). The baker can't tell who is grabbing Job, so the moment doesn't make sense. The BSB capitalizes 'He' in Job 30:18-19 for God.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The setup points the baker back to Job taking his seat in the public square (Job 29:7-10). A baker reasoning from that callback would pick 'market', a public gathering place like the square, over 'assembly'. The setup leads away from the right answer (Job 30:28), so getting it right comes down to knowing the wording, not reasoning.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from any verse, but it cites Job 30:31. Card 19 already cites that verse. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, which here is none.
findings.question: What should a last story card cite when it is only the 'story continues' line and tells no verse? The last verse of the passage, the passage's whole range, or nothing?
